name: cling
why: An interactive C++ interpreter from CERN that makes a famously compiled language feel like a REPL playground.

brief.what_it_is: Cling is an interactive C++ interpreter built on Clang and LLVM. You type C++ at a command prompt, or pass it as arguments, and it compiles each piece just-in-time and runs it, with compiler diagnostics printed back to you. It has an emacs-style line editor, dot-prefixed metaprocessor commands for loading files, libraries and include paths, and a Jupyter kernel. The README describes it as implementing the read-eval-print loop concept for rapid application development.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says one of Cling's main goals was to provide a contemporary, high-performance alternative to CINT, the first C++ interpreter in the ROOT project, with backward compatibility with CINT as a major priority. The README frames it as bringing a REPL to C++ for rapid application development.
brief.how_it_works: Cling is a small extension to LLVM and Clang: Clang parses the input and LLVM's just-in-time compiler generates code that runs inside the interpreter process. On startup it automatically includes several header files and its own runtime universe, which creates the minimal environment for the user to begin. The README also says it reuses Clang's concise, expressive compiler diagnostics.

brief.install_notes: The Homebrew formula is cling and installs an executable named cling. The GitHub README says nightly binary snapshots are currently unavailable, so building from source is the main route it documents. Building as a standalone project requires a build of Clang and LLVM from the root-project/llvm-project repository on the cling-latest branch, configured with cmake using LLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD="host;NVPTX". Cling can also be built together with LLVM using LLVM_EXTERNAL_PROJECTS. Do not build inside the source directories. Jupyter support needs a separate install following the README in tools/Jupyter, and cling must be on PATH when jupyter starts.
brief.standout: Cling is a REPL for a compiled language built on the real Clang front end, so it accepts C++ and reports errors the way the compiler does. Its metaprocessor dot-commands and its CINT-compatibility goal set it apart from simpler C++ REPLs.
brief.status: unknown. I saw no release date or last commit. The GitHub README says nightly binaries are currently unavailable and that some linked resources are rather old and most of the stated limitations are outdated. It does document a release process with tags and release notes, and the Homebrew formula is present.
brief.caveats: The README warns that some resources are old and the stated limitations are outdated. Nightly binaries are unavailable, so you will likely need to build Clang and LLVM yourself, which is a heavy build. Contributors must transfer copyright to the Cling project. Debugging and profiling support has a runtime cost and is disabled by default. I did not read the LICENSE file. The supported platforms were not stated in the pages I read.
